title: Research on the Design of Financial Data Analysis Platform with Joint PSO-HQCNN and RPA Robot Visualization Technology
journal_or_venue: IEIE Transactions on Smart Processing and Computing
abstract_summary: The paper proposes an RPA-based financial data analysis platform that integrates a Hybrid Quantum Convolutional Neural Network (HQCNN) with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to convert classical data into quantum states and perform joint optimization. HQCNN shows lower loss and improved training/test accuracy versus a classical CNN, while PSO-HQCNN attains the highest recognition accuracy (96.85%) but incurs substantially longer training time. The study also demonstrates RPA robot visualization and automated report generation for enterprise financial analysis.
methodology_description: The study develops an RPA-driven financial data analysis platform and evaluates hybrid quantum-classical neural network models for automated visual recognition tasks within that platform. The methodological pipeline begins with acquisition of financial-system CAPTCHA-style images (4-character images). Images are preprocessed by segmenting characters using a pixel-projection method (column-wise nonzero pixel counts) with a threshold of 13 and isometric splitting when segment width > 30; badly segmented samples are manually removed. Classical image arrays are resized/compressed for quantum-bit encoding (paper states compression to size "82" in quantum bit coding mode) and pixel values normalized to [0,1], then remapped to angles in [0, π/2] for conversion into quantum state encodings. The core model is a Hybrid Quantum Convolutional Neural Network (HQCNN) that combines a parameterized quantum convolutional layer (built from double-qubit gates U and single-qubit rotation R gates whose angular parameters are learnable) with classical pooling (max-pooling) and classical fully-connected layers; cross-entropy loss is computed from single-qubit measurement probabilities. A particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is integrated with HQCNN (PSO-HQCNN) for joint optimization of the quantum-layer parameters. Baselines include a classical CNN and the HQCNN without PSO. Models are trained and compared over multiple iterations (loss/accuracy tracked for 100 iterations), with convergence behavior, loss stability, recognition accuracy, and training time reported. Results include per-model loss, training and test accuracies, recognition accuracy, and an application-level measurement of the automatic identification success rate (182/200 = 91%).

results_summary: The authors introduce a hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural network (HQCNN) and a PSO-augmented variant (PSO-HQCNN) within an RPA robot visualization framework for financial data analysis. In their experiments the HQCNN outperformed a classical CNN by small margins in loss (0.0056% lower) and accuracy (+0.93% training, +0.36% test), and showed earlier convergence and reduced loss fluctuation after 60–90 iterations. PSO-HQCNN achieved the highest recognition accuracy (96.85%) but required substantially longer training (23.6 hours) compared to HQCNN and CNN. The authors also report a 91% success rate (182/200) for an automatic identification task. Broader claims about inherent quantum advantages are presented but not empirically established on quantum hardware.

HQCNN convergence requires many iterations (loss stabilizes after ~90 iterations), implying non-trivial training time and tuning.
